newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stark says Germany will meet deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Stark says Germany will meet deficit goal.

text.p: German state secretary in the finance ministry Juergen Stark warned on Thursday that the Maastricht Treaty criteria must be adhered to strictly but said there was no doubt Germany would meet these goals.

At a breakfast meeting hosted by a local Christian Democrat group, Stark said "The criteria were not anchored in the Maastricht Treaty only for us then to depart from them. We want to take them seriously and we must take them seriously."
Stark is the latest German official to weigh into the raging debate about the Maastricht Treaty criteria which call for strict adherence to low budget deficits and reduced government debt.

Germany has traditionally followed a hardline interpretation of the Treaty but as Bonn itself is having trouble fulfilling the criteria for EMU entry, there have been some questions about whether Germany might not be prepared to take an easier line on the interpretation.
But Stark, sticking by statements he has made for months, insisted,"We shall meet the deficit criterion. There is no doubt about that," adding "I don't know where this doubt is coming from."

Some independent economists expressed doubt that Germany would meet the three percent deficit target range, particularly as Germany was still struggling with stubbornly high unemployment rates, costing the government considerable funds.
Stark also said that a monetary union with only some EU states as members would not be divisive for Europe.

German officials have often said they would prefer monetary union to begin only with those nations that absolutely meet the criteria so that the future currency euro could be at least as stable as the mark.
